question: Is the KV residency sampling too coarse, and do session 1 and session 2 evict simultaneously near Perfetto seconds 46.2–46.4?

configuration_profile.clock: Retained derived Perfetto clock; first normal input is at 40.071 seconds. User-selected run/track confirmation was requested; analysis assumes the current retained trace.
configuration_profile.sampler: OMNI_STATLOG_PERIOD_S=0.2; shared Scheduler.schedule hook, not an independent timer.

change: Audit and measurement documentation only; no sampler, engine or derived artifact changed.

sampling_intervals_ms.population: 111 intervals between normal-phase residency rows after the first normal tick; rounded exported timestamps, p95 sorted index round((n-1)*0.95)

target_window.interpretation: Both are already at 128 in the 46.2–46.4 window; the current trace does not show simultaneous falls there.

code_semantics: A single sample gives every live session the same timestamp; independently timed mutations between samples can become simultaneous counter changes.
SessionManager.advance independently considers all idle sessions and has no mutual-exclusion rule forbidding two sessions from being evicted close together.

Residency samples count request-owned block IDs or, without request ownership, the contiguous cached prefix. They are neither per-session watts nor a complete count of arbitrary disjoint/in-flight GPU blocks.
The power.draw field in gpu.csv is device-level; current trace does not provide per-session power attribution.

remaining_uncertainty: The user may be viewing a different run or track; the exact-window conclusion is conditional on the current retained Perfetto trace.
This audit identifies sampling limitations and two evictions, not general eviction correctness.
No finer sampling or event-driven physical-residency accounting has been implemented in this audit.
